result: In 7 NIH Neuro-PASC patients re-tested after more than 1 year, 71% of initially abnormal results stayed abnormal, including CSF indices of central catecholamine deficiency, CSF/serum oligoclonal bands, baroreflex-cardiovagal failure and tilt-evoked hypotension.
reason: Same NIH CSF catechol-deficiency measure in a long COVID cohort, adding persistence over time; n=7, so weak.

result: In 7 Neuro-PASC patients re-tested after more than 1 year, baroreflex-cardiovagal dysfunction and tilt-evoked sudden hypotension persisted (71% of initially abnormal tests stayed abnormal).
reason: Objective autonomic testing in long COVID; adds that the abnormalities persist past a year; very small n.

result: Of 92 children with long COVID in a rehabilitation clinic, 71% met criteria for an orthostatic condition (POTS, orthostatic tachycardia, classic or delayed OH, orthostatic hypertension) on a 10-min passive stand.
reason: Long COVID population and pooled orthostatic conditions with no separate POTS rate, so it does not test ME/CFS POTS prevalence; fits objective autonomic testing in long COVID (paediatric).

result: Of 92 children with long COVID, 71% met criteria for an orthostatic condition on a 10-min passive standing test.
reason: Reports no pulse-pressure or recent-onset subgroup data and does not assess lean-test validity; it is a long COVID orthostatic prevalence result.

result: Post-infectious ME/CFS had higher axial diffusivity in association and projection fibres (linked to worse physical scores), while gradual-onset ME/CFS had lower AD in the corpus callosum, compared with sedentary matched controls.
reason: Already cited: this is the preprint of Yu 2025 (Sci Rep), whose identical PI-vs-GO AD result is in the finding detail.

result: Among 534 ME/CFS patients with normal HR/BP tilt responses (vs 49 HC), 91% had abnormal CO and CBF reductions with a CO-CBF slope near 1, CO reduction mainly predicting CBF reduction; the 9% within the control range were milder and more often male.
reason: Same tilt CBF measure in normal-HR/BP patients, adding a mechanism (CO-driven, no cerebral compensatory vasodilation) and a severity/sex subgroup; same Dutch clinic, not independent.

result: Among 534 ME/CFS patients with normal HR/BP tilt responses, 91% had abnormal CO and CBF reductions with a near 1:1 CO-CBF relation.
reason: Already cited: the finding detail already includes van Campen 2024 for the roughly 1:1 CO-CBF relation.

result: In 475 adults 2-3 years after hospitalisation for COVID-19 (PHOSP-COVID/C-Fog), cognitive scores averaged 0.71 SD below expected, and psychiatric and cognitive symptoms rose over time through worsening and new onset; occupation change was linked mainly to cognitive deficits.
reason: Post-hospitalisation cohort with no ME/CFS case definition; it does not measure ME/CFS incidence or course, and the population is unlike the ME/CFS cognition finding.

result: On one week of actigraphy, 31 ME/CFS and 23 post-COVID ME/CFS patients showed lower activity and worse sleep quality than 31 matched controls, with no difference between the two patient groups.
reason: Objective (actigraphy) sleep worse in ME/CFS, in the same direction; small and gives no specific sleep parameters.

result: ME/CFS and post-COVID ME/CFS patients had higher endothelin-1 and VCAM-1 than matched controls (n=54 vs 31), and ICAM-1 tracked plasma lipids in controls only.
reason: The finding claims no consistent rise in endothelial-activation proteins; a raised ET-1 and VCAM-1 result runs against that (it sides with the smaller ELISA studies), so it is not a replication.
